items.title: Serre criterion for affineness
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The proof constructs global functions from the H1 vanishing hypothesis and obtains affine principal neighbourhoods. It then combines a finite principal-open cover with a unit-ideal argument to prove affineness; the covering construction is part of the problem rather than an assumed affineness criterion.

items.title: Chow lemma for separated finite-type morphisms over a Noetherian base
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.difficulty_reason: The proof constructs a quasi-projective proper modification of a separated finite-type scheme over a Noetherian base using closures of diagonal graph maps. Scheme-theoretic density permits gluing the local projections and proves exact inverse-image identities; these verify properness, surjectivity and a dense-open isomorphism. This is a substantive geometric construction beyond routine qualifying algebra.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Exactly the nontrivial positive-slope branch of Theorem4.1: 0<q<1, u>0 with positive roots chosen, n>=2 and n prime>0 coprime, sigma=[[m prime,m],[n prime,n]] in SL2(Z). On the full charged n-fermion Clifford module F^{n psi}, the currents (4.4) and H_k^{tw} act as Diff_q with c=n,c prime=n prime and identify the module with M_u^sigma. M_u is the full charged level-one fermion module (direct sum of Fock charge sectors), so this does not assert that the whole space is a single irreducible F_u^sigma. original_metadata.statement_scope: Exactly Theorem5.1: G is a compact Lie group, K a closed subgroup, and the natural G-action on T^*(G/K) is generically locally free with finite principal stabilizer H. No assertion at singular strata or without the locally free action hypothesis, and no separate metric-integrability corollary, is selected.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Exactly Theorem1.6 for every real nu>-1. M^(nu) is the projective probability measure on infinite positive-definite complex Hermitian matrices whose N-corner density is the normalized det(X)^(-nu-2N)*exp(-2*Tr(X^-1)) on H^+(N). In the Pickrell–Olshanski–Vershik parametrization, its spectral measure is supported on Omega_0^+: every negative alpha vanishes, all positive alpha_i are nonzero, gamma_2=0, and gamma_1=sum_i alpha_i^+<infinity. The positive parameters form the determinantal process on (0,infinity) with Lebesgue kernel K_infty^nu(x,y)=8/(x*y)*J_nu(8/x,8/y), where J_nu is the exact Bessel kernel of Definition1.5. No infinite-mass inverse-Wishart parameter range, real-matrix analogue or Hua–Pickrell trace result is asserted.

items.difficulty_reason: A refuter output need not reveal the truth of its SAT instance efficiently, so a single use of the refuter does not yield the desired contradiction. The proof recursively packages the complement of a longer instance into a smaller-input circuit, applies refuters across a shrinking sequence of lengths, and resolves the final instance using a hardcoded truth table. It coordinates the opposing input-size and refuter-size constraints using c < k squared, controlling all stages and the final table so that the constructed deciding circuit is itself small enough to be refuted.
